text:
sara: heads-up — customer 'fastchat' opened an escalation: p99 gen latency jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms around 03:20 UTC. seeing it in prod and the dedicated pool. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/fastchat/slo

dmitri: on it, thanks. do we have a kernel change around that time? any recent rollout of flashattn flags or SDPA fallback?

alan: there was a compileflag push to the attn kernels at 03:05 (optimize/simd-32 -> on by default). rollout to canary passed, then staged to all by 03:15. I flagged it for risk but it matched perf tests.

marie: quick numbers from infra: p95 went 130->280ms, p99 120->420ms, tail tokens/sec dropped by ~35% for seq_length=1024 requests. CPU on host didn't spike, GPU SM util slightly higher but memory traffic increased.

support-esc: customer provided a repro: model=gpt-neox-20b, seq=1024, batch=8, streaming=off. repro script attached in ticket.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: "compileflag-optimize-simd-32" rolled to pool:dedicated-3 at 03:15 UTC by alan.

alan: ok that matches. suggestion: toggle the new flag off on the dedicated pool for that customer and measure. can we hot toggle?

dmitri: yes there's a runtime kernel_selector override. quick command: 
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/pools/dedicated-3/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"kernel_selector": "legacy_attn", "reason": "p99 regression investig"}'
```
I'll run it for fastchat customer subset first.

alan: also add an exp compile log flag to capture kernel choice and fallback reasons. last time we were blind.

marie: adding logs now. toggled KV_CACHE_STATS too.

sara: ran quick smoke after toggle -> p99 dropped to ~150ms in ~6 mins. customer confirmed latency improved. they want RCA.

support-esc: they asked if we can confirm whether flashattn or SDPA was root cause. they saw retries and a few 500s.

dmitri: from traces: a subset of requests hit a new codepath where memory copy paths increased and we lost continuous-batching alignment -> significantly worse kernel launch churn. kernel names show: attn_opt_simd32 followed by fallback kernels 'attn_sdpa_fallback' in ~18% of heads. that's suspicious.

alan: hmm fallback in production suggests the new optimization triggered incompatible runtime path for some model dims. need compare kernel compile flags: gcc opts and CUDA arch flags might be different between canary and prod builds.

marie: I pulled compile artifacts. canary used nvcc -gencode=...sm_80 while prod used sm_86 build for the pool (heterogeneous hosts). the new simd32 kernel is only tuned for sm_80; on sm_86 it falls back to SDPA path.

dmitri: that explains mismatch. when a job is scheduled onto an sm_86 node it hits suboptimal fallback path. scheduler drift caused mixed-host assignment.

alan: mitigation plan: 1) pin dedicated-3 to legacy kernel selector until we release arch-aware kernels; 2) add a quick scheduler defense to prefer sm_80 for that pool; 3) build simd32 kernels for sm_86.

sara: action items recorded. support notified customer and offered a 3-day credits for impact.

support-esc: customer appreciated the quick toggle. they asked for timeline on proper fix.

alan: ETA for arch-aware builds: repro, compile, test across sm_80/sm_86 and run perf harness -> ~48hrs. can push a hotfix to only enable simd32 when kernel arch match detected at runtime sooner (few hrs) if we add a guard.

dmitri: I'll follow up with a runtime guard: if device.compute_capability != kernel.target arch -> force legacy_attn and emit telemetry. can PR today and rollout to canary.

marie: I've already started instrumenting the selection path; logs will include device cc and compile tag.

ops-bot: ticket #ESC-5421 created and linked to customer 'fastchat'.

alan: retrospective note: our canary pool lacked sm_86 nodes so the canary pass missed cross-arch issues — need to add heterogeneity coverage to perf tests. adding to roadmap.

sara: for RCA summary (to include in customer-facing note): root cause = new simd32 attn compileflag rolled to mixed-arch pool; on sm_86 devices it fell back to SDPA/slow fallback kernel causing p99 spike; mitigation = runtime toggle to legacy_attn + scheduler pin; long-term fix = arch-targeted kernel builds and runtime guard.

support-esc: customer update prepared, sending now. closing thread after follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
